Hi Asha — following up with a concise written explanation and sample math so your procurement team has something to attach to the packet. I also included two quick scenarios based on the character export you mentioned (attached CSV).

1) Tokens vs characters vs requests (brief):
- Billing unit: Redwood bills by tokens (input tokens + output tokens consumed by the model). We do not bill per request; request count is used for rate limiting and quota but not the primary billing unit.
- Characters: character counts are just a convenient export metric. For English text a useful conversion is: ~4 characters per token (this is an average — your data will vary with punctuation, languages, and long identifiers). We include an automatic converter in the console.
- Requests: number of API calls. Helpful for estimating RPS and concurrency, not directly for $ calculation.

2) Prompt caching vs billed tokens (how it works in practice):
- Redwood supports prefix/KV caching. If a full prompt+response pair is served entirely from the cache (exact match), the request is served from cache storage and there is no model re-run for that response — in that case you are not billed for model compute tokens for the cached response.
- For partial cache hits (cached prefix but new completion tokens requested), you are billed for the tokens that the model actually generates (the uncached suffix) and for any input tokens the runtime must still process.
- Caching reduces both latency and billed model tokens when cache hits are complete; it reduces billed tokens proportionally when hits are partial.

3) Example conversion & unit economics (based on your CSV sample attached):
- You said your analytics show 180M characters/month across all workflows. Using 1 token ≈ 4 chars -> ~45M tokens/month.
- You estimated that ~70% of that is prompt (input) and ~30% is generation (output) for your flows -> prompt tokens: 31.5M, generated tokens: 13.5M, total = 45M tokens.

If your target pricing is in the $15–$45 per 1M tokens band, here are three quick scenarios (model-neutral):
- Low: $15 / 1M tokens -> monthly cost = 45 * $15 = $675
- Mid: $25 / 1M tokens -> monthly cost = 45 * $25 = $1,125
- High: $45 / 1M tokens -> monthly cost = 45 * $45 = $2,025

4) Impact of caching (conservative estimate):
- You said ~30% repeated prefixes for the agent flow and near 100% repeat for the email-summary template. If we assume 40% of total requests are fully cacheable responses, those cached responses would not incur model compute charges when served from cache.
- Adjusted token consumption with 40% full cache hit rate: billed tokens = 45M * (1 - 0.40) = 27M tokens/month.
- Example cost at mid price ($25 / 1M): 27 * $25 = $675/month. Note this is illustrative — exact savings depend on cache TTL, key granularity (per-user vs global template), and the fraction of responses fully identical.

5) Request bundling & batching:
- For many short prompts we recommend continuous batching at the runtime level (small batch windows to preserve latency). Batching reduces GPU overhead and can lower unit price for high-throughput flows. We can model latency tradeoffs; Sean can share the recommended batching window for your 500ms SLO.

- Asha: if you can share the CSV export (characters per message + request counts) we will produce a 1‑page cost table at low/mid/high, and a caching-sensitivity column showing expected savings at 0/20/40/60% cache hit rates.
- Marissa: I will need a short note about VPC/private deployment pricing and SLA add-on that we can attach to procurement.
